|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618230252/http://www.guhoyas.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111317aac.html |url-status=dead }} (born January 6, 1999) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bàsquet Girona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[FIBA Europe Cup]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown Hoyas]] and the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]]. He was a consensus three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and among the highest-ranked high school players in [[Virginia]]. He is one of two players to be a three-time [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] champion, alongside [[Nate Robinson]], and the only player to win three consecutive Slam Dunk Contests. McClung went unselected in the [[2021 NBA draft]] and spent time during the 2021–22 season with the [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He won the 2021–22 [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award|NBA G League Rookie of the Year]] award with the South Bay Lakers of the G League. McClung joined the Blue Coats for the 2022–23 season and signed with the 76ers in February 2023. He won the [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] at the [[2023 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|2023]], [[2024 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|2024]], and [[2025 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|2025 NBA All-Star Game]]. He has earned the 2024 and 2026 [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award]], and holds the record for the most points scored in G League History. ==Early life== McClung grew up in [[Gate City, Virginia]], a small town of about 2,000 in the [[Tri-Cities, Tennessee|Tri-Cities metropolitan area]] straddling the [[Tennessee]]–Virginia border, where he initially began playing [[American football|football]]—a sport that is far more popular than basketball in [[Southwest Virginia]].{{cite web|first=Ava|last=Wallace|title=Country Star|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2018/03/01/feature/mac-mcclung-has-dunked-past-allen-iverson-and-will-follow-him-to-georgetown/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=March 1, 2018|access-date=June 18, 2018}} Family members recalled in a 2018 interview that McClung was extraordinarily competitive as a child. His father Marcus said of him, "Mac was just born with it. If you’re fixing a bowl of cereal, he’s going to make a competition." His older sister Anna would add, "He would just come at you every day, no matter how small he was." His parents built a basement gym in their home, initially for Anna, but Mac would regularly use it as he grew up—though he was so competitive that his father would frequently ban him from the gym to allow Anna to work out undisturbed.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Palmer|title=Georgetown Freshman Mac McClung Is Electrifying, Dynamic – and White|url=https://andscape.com/features/georgetown-freshman-mac-mcclung-is-electrifying-dynamic-and-white/|website=Andscape.com|date=July 13, 2018|access-date=July 14, 2018}} He received his first significant exposure to basketball just before entering the seventh grade, when his mother Lenoir signed him up for a local youth league. Scott Vermillion, who was McClung's coach at [[Gate City High School]], recalled in 2018, "He ducked his head inside for a minute and basically never left." McClung soon became more interested in basketball and began training for the sport regularly, with hopes of making the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA),{{cite web |last=Hazan |first=Danny |date=July 21, 2017 |title=Arrival of the Mac |url=https://www.slamonline.com/slam-tv/arrival-of-the-mac/ |access-date=December 14, 2024 |work=[[Slam (magazine)|SLAM]]}} and his father was silently pleased when he gave up football after his freshman year of high school. According to McClung, his shooting form improved after he broke his arm while [[snowboarding]] in eighth grade, and he honed the skill with Greg Ervin, the former head coach at Gate City High. ==High school career== McClung first started [[Slam dunk|dunking]] as a sophomore playing varsity basketball at Gate City High School. He grew in profile as an acrobatic dunker through the rest of his high school career. [[MaxPreps]] labeled him "one of nation's most exciting players." As a junior, on February 24, 2017, he scored a career-high 64 points in a loss to Dan River High School at the [[Virginia High School League]] (VHSL) Region 2A West tournament.{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Hayes|title=McClung's 64 points not enough for Gate City in Region 2A West boys He ended his high school career with Gate City's first state championship, scoring 47 points in an 80–65 title-game win over [[Staunton, Virginia|Staunton]]'s [[Robert E. Lee High School (Staunton, Virginia)|Robert E. Lee High]]. state title|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2018/mac-mcclung-drops-47-leads-gate-city-to-first-state-title|work=[[USA Today]]|date=March 10, 2018|access-date=June 19, 2018}} McClung finished the season (2018–2020)=== On December 22, 2018, McClung scored a freshman season-high 38 points for Georgetown in a 102–94 victory over [[2018–19 Little Rock Trojans men's basketball team|Little Rock]].{{cite web |title=Little Rock at Georgetown Box Score, Dec 22, 2018 |url=https://guhoyas.com/sports/mens-basketball/stats/2018-19/little-rock/boxscore/12556 |access-date=December 14, 2024 |website=GUHoyas.com}} As a freshman, he averaged 13.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and two assists per game, leading [[Big East Conference]] freshmen in scoring. McClung was named to the Big East All-Freshman Team.{{cite web |date=March 10, 2019 |title=Govan Named All-Big East First Team; Akinjo, LeBlanc and McClung to All-Freshman Team |url=https://guhoyas.com/news/2019/3/10/mens-basketball-govan-named-all-big-east-first-team-akinjo-leblanc-and-mcclung-to-all-freshman-team.aspx |access-date=May 27, 2020 |website=GUHoyas.com}} In February 2020, during his sophomore season, he missed several games with a foot injury.{{cite news |last=Curran |first=Aidan |date=February 9, 2020 |title=With Blair Improving, What Do The Hoyas Do When McClung Returns? |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgetown/Article/With-Blair-Improving-What-Do-The-Hoyas-Do-When-McClung-Returns-143602774/ |access-date=February 16, 2020 |work=247 Sports}} McClung only played 21 games due to the injury, averaging 15.7 points, 2.4 assists and 1.4 steals in 27 minutes per game as a sophomore. After the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] and signed with an NCAA-certified agent to maintain his collegiate eligibility.{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=March 29, 2020 |title=Georgetown's Mac McClung to test draft waters |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28968201 |access-date=March 29, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]]}} On May 13, he withdrew from the draft and entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=May 13, 2020 |title=Georgetown's Mac McClung to withdraw from NBA draft process, enter transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29170757 |access-date=May 13, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]]}} ===Texas Tech (2020–2021)=== [[File:NCAA Basketball- Texas Tech at Louisiana State - 50892322513.jpg|thumb|McCLung with the Raiders basketball team in 2021]] On May 27, 2020, McClung left Georgetown and announced that he would transfer to [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Boone|title=Mac McClung transfer: Former Georgetown guard chooses Texas Tech as destination|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mac-mcclung-transfer-former-georgetown-guard-chooses-texas-tech-as-destination/|work=CBS Sports|date=May 27, 2020|access-date=May 27, 2020}} He was granted a waiver for immediate eligibility on October 30.{{cite news |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=October 30, 2020 |title=Texas Tech guard Mac McClung receives waiver to play basketball immediately |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30223714 |access-date=October 30, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]]}} In his Texas Tech debut on November 25, McClung scored 20 points in a 101–58 win against [[2020–21 Northwestern State Demons basketball team|Northwestern State]].{{cite news|title=No. 14 Texas Tech opens with 101–58 win over Northwestern St|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401259558|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 25, 2020|access-date=November 26, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 15.5 points, 2.7 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game. McClung entered the transfer portal again in April 2021 while simultaneously declaring for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 11, 2021 |title=Mac McClung leaving Texas Tech, to test NBA draft, transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31239004 |access-date=May 17, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}} In May 2021, McClung confirmed via [[Twitter]] that he would remain in the draft and forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=May 17, 2021 |title=Texas Tech guard Mac McClung to sign with agent, remain in NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31460965 |access-date=May 17, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}} ==Professional career== ===South Bay Lakers (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], McClung joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]],{{cite web|title=Lakers Announce 2021 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-announce-summer-league-2021-roster|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021}} and signed afterward with the team on August 10, 2021.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. and Mac McClung|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-and-mac-mcclung-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2021|access-date=September 3, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 13.{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Mac McClung|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-waive-mac-mcclung-211013|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 14, 2021}} On October 23, 2021, he signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]], the affiliate team of the Los Angeles Lakers. McClung's debut with South Bay consisted of a game-high 24 points, nine assists and six rebounds in a 112–105 victory over the [[NBA G League Ignite]] on November 5, 2021.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kioski|title=South Bay Finalizes Training Camp Roster|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} ===Chicago / Windy City Bulls (2021–2022)=== On December 22, 2021, McClung signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Bulls Sign Mac McClung To 10-Day Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/12/bulls-to-sign-mac-mcclung-to-a-10-day-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} He signed a second 10-day contract with them on January 1, 2022.{{cite news |date=January 1, 2022 |title=Bulls' Mac McClung: Signs second 10-day contract |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bulls-mac-mcclung-signs-second-10-day-contract/ |access-date=January 1, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}} On January 4, 2022, the Chicago Bulls assigned McClung to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite news|title=Bulls assign McClung to their G League team|url=https://www.timesnews.net/sports/bulls-assign-mcclung-to-their-g-league-team/article_c2392d98-6dce-11ec-9028-5b538093cc36.html|work=[[Kingsport Times-News]]|date=January 4, 2022|access-date=January 7, 2022}} McClung debuted the next night, scoring 19 points and adding nine assists in a 112–108 loss to the [[Motor City Cruise]]. On January 6, 2022, McClung was recalled to the main roster.{{cite news|first=P. Kevin|last=Mays|title=Bulls recall Gate City native McClung|url=https://www.timesnews.net/sports/bulls-recall-gate-city-native-mcclung/article_1f246c56-6f3d-11ec-8900-434449616a2c.html|work=[[Kingsport Times-News]]|date=January 6, 2022|access-date=January 7, 2022}} ===Return to South Bay / Los Angeles Lakers (2022)=== On January 11, 2022, after his 10-day contracts expired, McClung was reacquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 10, 2022}} He was named the 2021–22 [[NBA G League Rookie of the Year Award|G League Rookie of the Year]].{{cite web |date=April 9, 2022 |title=South Bay Lakers' Mac McClung Named 2021-22 Kia NBA G League Rookie of the Year |url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-mac-mcclung-named-2021-22-kia-nba-g-league-rookie-of-the-year/ |access-date=April 9, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}{{cite web |last=Kasabian |first=Paul |date=April 9, 2022 |title=Lakers Rumors: Mac McClung to Sign 2-Way Contract After G League Stint |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10032141-lakers-rumors-mac-mcclung-to-sign-2-way-contract-after-g-league-stint |access-date=April 9, 2022 |website=BleacherReport.com}} On April 9, 2022, McClung signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite tweet|author=Los Angeles Lakers|title=OFFICIAL: The Lakers have signed @McclungMac to a two-way contract. McClung averaged 21.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 7.6 assists for the @SouthBayLakers this season.|number=1512847251491618818|user=Lakers|date=April 9, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022}} On June 29, Los Angeles declined his $1.62 million qualifying offer, making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web|title=Mac McClung|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/los-angeles-lakers/mac-mcclung-74267/|website=Spotrac.com|access-date=July 11, 2022}}{{cite web | last=Schuhmann | first=John | title=2022 Free Agency: Options and qualifying offers | website=NBA | date=2022-08-20 | url=https://www.nba.com/news/2022-free-agency-options-and-qualifying-offers | access-date=2025-12-02}} He joined the Lakers for the [[California Classic]] in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|first=Zach|last=Zafran|title=Warriors add Lakers' G League Rookie of the Year Mac McClung to summer league roster|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-add-Lakers-Mac-McClung-17290312.php|work=SFGate.com|date=July 7, 2022|access-date=July 14, 2022}} After playing two games for the Lakers' summer league team, McClung joined the [[Golden State Warriors]]' summer squad. web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Mac McClung, Daeqwon Plowden and Brandon 2, he joined the [[Osceola Magic]].{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Just Dropped|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-just-dropped|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}} On February 17, 2024, McClung won the [[2024 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|2024 NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] for the second consecutive year, joining [[Michael Jordan]], [[Jason Richardson]], [[Nate Robinson]] and [[Zach LaVine]] as the only players to win back-to-back contests. Furthermore, he became the first and only player from a G-League team to win the contest, as he had been called up by the 76ers a day before the previous year's contest. On April 5, he was named [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award|NBA G League Most Valuable Player]] after averaging 25.7 points, 4.7 rebounds and 6.6 assists in 27 games while scoring 30-plus points in eight of them.{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic's Mac McClung Named 2023-24 Kia NBA G League Most Valuable Player|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/osceola-magics-mac-mcclung-named-2023-24-kia-nba-g-league-most-valuable-player|website=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2024|access-date=April 5, 2024}} On September 20, 2024, McClung re-signed with the [[Orlando Magic]]{{cite web |date=September 20, 2024 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agents Mac McClung, Javonte Smart and Ethan Thompson |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agents-mac-mcclung-javonte-smart-ethan-thompson-20240919 |access-date=September 20, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} and on October 19, his Exhibit 10 contract was converted into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Convert Contract of Mac McClung to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-convert-contract-of-mac-mcclung-to-two-way-contract-20241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}}{{cite web |date=October 19, 2024 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Magic give dunk champ Mac McClung two-way contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/41886243 |access-date=October 19, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}} On February 15th 2025, McClung won the NBA Slam Dunk Contest for the third consecutive year, scoring 50s on all of his dunks and becoming the first player ever to win three consecutive dunk contests. On February 15, 2025, McClung won the [[2025 NBA All-Star Game#Slam Dunk Contest|2025 NBA Slam Dunk Contest]], having four dunks that were scored a perfect 50 by the judges. McClung is the only player in NBA history to win the Slam Dunk Contest three years in a row. He also joined [[Nate Robinson]] as the only players in NBA history to win the contest three times.{{cite web|url= https://www.nba.com/magic/news/mac-mcclung-becomes-first-player-to-win-nba-all-star-slam-dunk-contest-in-three-straight-years-20250215|title= Mac McClung Becomes First Player to Win NBA All-Star Slam Dunk Contest in Three Straight Years |website=nba.com|last=Cohen|first=Josh|date=February 15, 2025|access-date=February 16, 2025}} McClung re-signed with the Chicago Bulls on October 17, 2025. Just three hours later, the Bulls waived McClung, replacing him with [[Trentyn Flowers]].{{Cite web |last=Toledo |first=Martin |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Mac McClung's 3-Hour Bulls Nightmare: Why Chicago Signed Him Then Axed Him Before He Even Unpacked |url=https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/mac-mcclungs-3-hour-bulls-nightmare-why-chicago-signed-him-then-axed-him-before-he-even-unpacked-1748592 |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=International Business Times UK}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=October 18, 2025 |title=Mac McClung's Chicago Bulls chapter ends before it begins after being waived just three hours after signing |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/nba/top-stories/mac-mcclungs-chicago-bulls-chapter-ends-before-it-begins-after-being-waived-just-three-hours-after-signing/articleshow/124653124.cms |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=Times of India}} === Indiana Pacers (2025) === On October 27, 2025, McClung was signed to a multi-year contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |last1=Charania |first1=Shams |title=Pacers to sign dunk champion Mac McClung, cut James Wiseman |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46749598/pacers-sign-dunk-champion-mac-mcclung-cut-james-wiseman |website=ESPN |date=October 27, 2025 |access-date=27 October 2025}} On October 29, he made his Pacers debut against the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]], and in 13 minutes, he finished with seven points, two rebounds, one assist, two steals, and one block while also going 1-for-3 from the three-point line.{{cite web | last=Hayes| first=Tim| title=NBA: Mac McClung (Gate City) scored seven points in his first game with the Pacers on Wednesday. Will it be the start of an extended stay in Indiana for the 26-year-old? | website=The Bristol Herald Courier | date=2025-10-30 | url=https://heraldcourier.com/sports/high-school/basketball/article_e7f56767-e0ae-4aa5-a8b8-1fc1dc8344f9.html | access-date=2025-12-13}}{{cite web |last=ESPN |title=Mac McClung – Indiana Pacers Guard |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4397071/mac-mcclung |website=ESPN |access-date=October 29, 2025}} In three appearances for Indiana, he averaged 6.3 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists in 11.3 minutes. On November 6, McClung was waived by Indiana after the team signed [[Monté Morris]].{{Cite web|title=Mac McClung Reportedly Waived by Pacers, Monte Morris to Join Roster on New Contract|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25285739-mac-mcclung-reportedly-waived-pacers-monte-morris-join-roster-new-contract|access-date=November 6, 2025|website=bleacherreport.com|language=en}} === Return to Chicago / Windy City Bulls (2025–2026) === On November 9, 2025, McClung joined the Windy City Bulls.{{Cite web|title=3-time NBA Slam Dunk Contest champ Mac McClung returns for second stint with Windy City Bulls|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/mac-mclung-returns-windy-city-bulls|access-date=December 31, 2025|website=cbsnews.com|language=en}} On February 5, 2026, the Bulls re-signed McClung to a two-way contract.{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bulls Sign Mac McClung to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-sign-mac-mcclung-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bulls shockingly add another guard with Mac McClung signing |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/onsi/news/chicago-bulls-shockingly-add-another-guard-with-mac-mcclung-signing-5 |access-date=2026-02-06 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}} The same day, McClung made his debut with the Bulls, scoring four points in 13 minutes; he also got one rebound, an assist, and a block to pair with his points.{{Cite web |title=New-look Bulls fall to Raptors, 123-107 |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/new-look-bulls-falls-to-raptors-123-107 |access-date=2026-02-07 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en-US}} Although it was announced that McClung wouldn't be participating in the [[2026 NBA All-Star Game|2026 Dunk Contest]],{{Cite web |title=Three-time Slam Dunk champ Mac McClung skipping 2026 contest |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47736944/three-slam-dunk-champ-mac-mcclung-skipping-2026-contest |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en-US}} he was announced as the replacement for [[David Jones García]] in the 2026 Castrol Rising Stars game.{{Cite web |title=Chicago’s McClung to replace San Antonio’s Jones-García in 2026 Castrol Rising Stars |url=https://www.nba.com/news/chicagos-mcclung-to-replace-san-antonios-jones-garcia-in-2026-castrol-rising-stars |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en-US}} On March 10, 2026, McClung scored 54 points with the [[Windy City Bulls]] against the [[College Park Skyhawks]], which is the fifth-highest scoring game in [[G League]] history. On March 24, he became the G-League's all-time leading scorer after scoring 59 points against the [[Birmingham Squadron]], the third highest scoring game in league history.{{cite news |author1=Kenny Hawkins |title=McClung becomes the all time leading scorer in NBA G-league history |url=https://www.wjhl.com/sports/local-sports/mcclung-becomes-the-all-time-leading-scorer-in-nba-g-league-history/ |access-date=25 March 2026 |work=WJHL.com |date=24 March 2026}} On April 3, 2026, McClung was named the MVP of the 2025–2026 NBA G League season. || .403 || .313 || .797 || 2.8 || 2.2 || 1.0 || .2 || 14.7 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== McClung is the son of Marcus McClung and Lenoir McClung. During his birth, his umbilical cord was [[Nuchal cord|tightly wrapped around his neck]]; his father recalled, "He was blue as a [[The Smurfs|Smurf]]." The attending physicians quickly freed him, and he almost immediately recovered. His parents met at [[Virginia Tech]], where Marcus played [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|football]]{{cite web |date=November 8, 2017 |title=Mac McClung signs to Georgetown Univ. |url=https://heraldcourier.com/gallery/mac-mcclung-signs-to-georgetown-univ/collection_596b0314-c4f3-11e7-b960-fbc794886050.html |access-date=December 14, 2024 |work=[[Bristol Herald Courier]]}}{{cite web|first=Toderrick|last=Hunt|title=Rutgers basketball commit Mac McClung has ties you won't believe, including 1 to a rapper|url=http://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/index.ssf/2017/08/rutgers_b-ball_commit_mac_mcclung_has_interesting.html|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=August 24, 2017|access-date=January 12, 2018}} and Lenoir was a cheerleader. His father became an attorney, serving as Commonwealth Attorney for [[Scott County, Virginia]] as of 2018, while his mother was teaching driver's education at Gate City High. According to a 2018 story in ''[[The Washington Post]]'', as well as a story in ''The Undefeated'', his parents' background aided McClung in his athletic pursuits. His father served as trainer for much of his youth, and the family was able to afford placing him on a [[Richmond, Virginia|Richmond]]-based [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] travel team. His sister Anna, who completed her high school [[Association football|soccer]] career as the VHSL's all-time goal scoring leader, played the sport at [[Florida State Seminoles women's soccer|Florida State]] and [[Tennessee Volunteers women's soccer|Tennessee]], and his uncle [[Seth McClung|Seth]] competed with two [[Major League Baseball]] (MLB) teams. His cousins [[Correne Bredin|Correne]] and Colette both played Division I college hockey and pro hockey; Correne also played with the Canadian national team.{{Cite web|url=https://hoopshd.com/2020/05/02/2020-draft-preview-hoopshd-interviews-georgetown-prospect-mac-mcclung/|title=2020 Draft Preview: HoopsHD interviews Georgetown prospect Mac McClung|last=Teitel|first=Jon|publisher=Hoops HD|quote=Your father Marcus played football at Virginia Tech, your sister Anna finished her high school soccer career as the with the most goals in state history, your uncle Seth played pro baseball, and your cousins Correne/Colette Bredin both played pro hockey: who is the best athlete in the family? I do not know: I think it is yet to be determined. It is hard to beat my cousin Correne making the Canadian Olympic team: that is a top-notch thing! |date=May 2, 2020|accessdate=February 16, 2025}} Although Houston rapper [[Riff Raff (rapper)|Riff Raff]] originally claimed that he is Mac McClung's cousin by way of their mothers being sisters, this has been denied by Mac McClung in an interview.{{cite web |date=May 17, 2018 |title=Mac McClung EXPOSED!!
